prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
Added the `tasklist` extension with its tests, docs and changelog entry. Its 7 new tests error with `No module named 'tasklist'` in the normal suite, because the short name needs the package reinstalled. I couldn't reinstall (`pip install -e .` was blocked by the sandbox). I ran the same tests with the full path `markdown.extensions.tasklist` and all 7 passed. The rest of the suite still passes. flake8 isn't installed, so I didn't lint.

The checkbox renders as `<input disabled="disabled" type="checkbox" /> text` by default. `checked` is added for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` is dropped when `clickable` is true. I left the space after the marker in the output rather than consuming it.

The entry point is registered in `pyproject.toml`, so `extensions=['tasklist']` should work once the package is reinstalled.
